plotSections.title: Invisibility and silence lifted
bullets: The party is no longer invisible or silent. Ord cast Dispel Magic, the crew could yell again, and the boat rocked. Before that they had been talking through their small communication items. Sylan says he and Aris, the two magical characters, ended it with magic.
Sylan is unsure whether the dispel was aimed at the spectral door or at an effect on the party. Dana says that if it had been on the door itself, she would expect the door to no longer lead anywhere.

plotSections.title: Phylactery hunt and the flight home
bullets: The party is still hunting a phylactery. The ship is flying back to Langdale Stronghold to meet Walker when he returns.
Sylan expects Carlkin and Benji may each have a lead once they arrive. If those turn up nothing, he expects the next stop is Nyx, which he does not want but thinks they will have to revisit.

plotSections.title: Walker at Haven Hold
bullets: Walker is leaving Hanzuni’s hoard room at Haven Hold. Hanzuni is the copper dragon and hoard master. Walker has not set a time to meet Elrus or Araden and is on his own running-track training schedule.
The regimen has left him with a level of exhaustion, so he has disadvantage on ability checks.
The party plans to regroup with him after about a week of their time. Under the sevenfold time difference, the DM figures that as roughly a month for Walker.

plotSections.title: The spectral door
bullets: A shut, corporeal, translucent, glowing spectral door with no frame and no writing follows the ship. The party has thought about opening it and has not.

Dana can see it, calls Gerk the doorman, and asks why he does not close it. Gerk says the door is over there and they are here, and that the last time he sank he turned invisible. He will not touch it aboard and does not want to fall off again.

Dana ties the door to Gerk’s Doorman role and to Ord having tried to open a door, or merely thought of one. She treats it as keystone-level magic and doubts a simple dispel would dismiss it, or that dispelling it would be the same as making it leave.

Sylan wonders whether using it again would open somewhere new. He and Dana agree not to test it while airborne. If it is still there they will try on solid ground, on the theory it might last a couple of hours and then could be reopened. Gerk may experiment only off the boat and will tell the others if anything happens.

About a day after it was opened, at roughly the same time of day, the door pops out of existence on its own. The party later reads the duration as at least about twenty-four hours. The space-altering effect is gone and the stern is empty. Gerk feels briefly less protected, then that feeling fades. He did not experiment with it. He checks a watch; after confusion about how to read it, the watch does move.

plotSections.title: Five days to Langdale
bullets: The voyage from Monta Valia to the stronghold takes five days through the Twin Peaks. It is casual and uneventful, with autumn on the mountains, snow creeping down from the heights, the first migratory herds, and no further door.

Langdale is in harvest. A familiar hut is ringed with manageable tomato fields. Trade caravans run between New Navel and the party’s tavern, with some traffic still to and from the Rita area. More fishing boats are on the glassy lake, and small crews are casting nets in the coves. The ship circles in and lands.

plotSections.title: Two days at the stronghold
bullets: Walker is about two days out, so the group staying behind has about two full days. He is treated as safe because he would have checked in six days ago if something were wrong.

Sylan proposes using the time to find Carlkin, who is believed to live in the tower, and Benji if he is in town, and to ask what they are hunting. Otherwise they can practice the doors indoors, away from people they do not trust. Sylan also plans to spend time with his relic and learn to use it better.
Sylan, Gerk, Ord, and Dana go to Carlkin. Walker stays behind.

plotSections.title: Grixto’s hideaway
bullets: Walker will meet Elrus and Araden and, once Plymouth Gawater finishes his errand, continue to the dragon-rider training grounds to investigate. Walker does not remember the lead they were chasing.

The grounds are the secret hideaway of a younger Grixto. He lured guild companions there, killed them, and took their Al Kurin—their dragons’ hearts of hearts—to amplify his power. He eventually killed Tunimus and a right hand whose name is not recalled, and that group later fell to Elrus and Araden.
The party knows the place from a vision Emhet gave essentially everyone, triggered through Dana by something like legend lore: Grixto sitting with a couple of Al Kurin and plotting his next steps.
Sylan’s instruction if Grixto is there: do not fight; both of them retreat.

plotSections.title: The training island
bullets: Walker, Araden, and Plymouth Gawater leave Sunder for a small floating island between the Lost Isles, Camp Two, and the Howling Tunnels. The trip is seven days for Walker and one day for the party staying behind.

The island looks ordinary: a broad flat field of thick grass, a crumbling foundation, and on the western plateau and cliffs the ruins of a stronghold. Caves in the cliffs are temporary dead-end roosts, from about a small horse stable up to the size of Araden’s roost entrance, enough for dragons that trained or rested here.
Elrus mind-whispers to Walker over the wind that the guild hall has crumbled from time and disuse, and he suspects Grixto’s cavern is reached from the back or underneath.

Walker’s Perception (21) confirms the cave systems sit on the underside, away from the training field. The Emhet vision showed people walking out of a humble dwelling as if looking for guests, not dropping out of a cave.

Where the rocky underside meets the field there is a thin crevice a medium dragon, possibly a large one, could squirm through, then hop onto the grass. An easy-to-miss footpath ledge runs from the training field down into that crack along the island’s rounded edge.

plotSections.title: Splitting at the crevice
bullets: Walker decides the crack is the place to start and goes in. Araden cannot fit. Glimmen would be a squeeze, and it is unknown whether she fits.

Plymouth is not on the mental link. He is studying expansive runes and wondering whether any artifacts remain after a long abandonment. Walker tells him not to wander far in case they need to leave quickly.

They split up. Plymouth will search the stronghold, then regroup at the crack, and Walker should holler if needed. Araden stays outside to raise a ruckus. Elrus stays outside as a mental relay: flag signals are useless without line of sight, so Walker should call with his mind. Elrus says he can intervene more effectively than Araden, who would take a long time to dig the crevice open. Walker is satisfied, and the scene pauses on him.

plotSections.title: Carlkin’s lighthouse
bullets: Ord, Sylan, Gerk, and Dana arrive in New Navel at a semi-familiar lighthouse they have entered once or twice. The door is aged, weathered wood. Posted signs, in mixed styles and several languages, include a no-loitering notice and one the party reads as appointments only.

Sylan jokes that they need an appointment and asks if Gerk can read. Gerk reads a sign as “Knock loud. Be let in.” and pounds the door. A roll of 12, which he treats as a 32, cracks the boards, squeaks the hinges, shifts the door like a struck sandbag, and shakes dust loose. After the third blow Carlkin shouts from inside to stop breaking his door. He says he does not know any “girls,” brushes them off, and says they have no appointment. Sylan remarks that he had forgotten Carlkin’s voice.

Gerk keeps hitting. A bolt slides, and the last blow throws the door open into a pile of crates and books. Carlkin, an elderly turtle who had been holding it, is slid backward, startled, confused, and furious. He says that is not what the signs say: he wrote them in sixteen languages, and asks what they want and why they cannot read.

Gerk says Sylan wanted to talk to him. Sylan calls Gerk their ambassador; Gerk mocks Sylan’s arms. Sylan says they have been dealing with stern matters, takes Carlkin for someone knowledgeable, admits he is not sure they have spoken before, and asks to discuss things of great importance. Carlkin refuses the vagueness and the lack of an appointment, says he is busy studying, and tries to push Gerk back. He has no leverage. Gerk walks in and Carlkin is shoved aside.

plotSections.title: Inside the lighthouse
bullets: The ground floor is piled with boxes, books, and supplies. A heap behind the door stops it dead, and barrels line the other wall. A spiral stair on the far wall goes up. Tables in the middle hold maps, tomes, and loose papers, including a first edition of the Sea of Nyx that the party had been part of, mixed with newer pages of many ages and very old tomes in no order. Porridge bowls are out, and a pile of books in the corner is snoring.

Before committing, Sylan asks Dana and Ord whether anything should be kept from Carlkin. Ord says Carlkin has been a useful resource and sees no reason to distrust him. Dana says he was one of the original holders and that they have no reason to hide. Sylan takes that as covering their relics, and they all go in.

The door swings shut behind them almost on its own; Gerk reaches for it and finds it already closing. Sylan says they have questions and knowledge to trade. Carlkin’s first question is still why they were banging on his door. He tells them to produce the knowledge and cut to the chase, because he has studying and other appointments.

plotSections.title: An undirected door
bullets: Before the conversation with Carlkin gets past why they came, Gerk opens a Door in the living room with no destination in mind. He hopes it is not the ocean and opens it slowly in case water comes through. The DM calls for a d100 and says Gerk is about to learn something about this ability. Gerk rolls 68. The table jokes that it nearly went badly and describes the result as all ocean, but the destination is not narrated before the scene shifts.
On the cut back, Sylan says his own door opens into Walker’s room, and the DM agrees. Gerk then grasps the latch of an unseen door and pulls.

plotSections.title: The unused roost
bullets: Walker descends a worn cliffside path about two feet wide, sheer drop on the left and a retaining wall on the right, into the crevice. Glimmen has to crawl and squeeze through. Getting out is easier: a younger dragon could tuck its wings, hop out, and fly, which is probably how Grixto used the place.

The tunnel is about thirty feet long, dry and musty, with wind and a draft outside. About twenty feet in it opens into a larger space, and the smell of fresh death and decay comes from that end. Over the mind link Glimmen says she thought the place was unused and that the death smells fresh. Walker agrees.

Walker contacts Elrus. Elrus says there has not been a trainee in centuries, that only one person used this place, that he did not know it was there until the vision Walker’s friend presented, and that nothing dead should be down there. Walker asks him to get Plymouth and meet him, then draws his bow and stalks on. Glimmen readies her fiery breath.
Walker’s passive Perception is 18. He hears faint humming and the light tapping of two different stones, one a softer thud than a clack, from the cavern ahead.

He and Glimmen both sneak at disadvantage because she is moving through the cave. Walker gets a 10; Glimmen gets a 19 that the DM counts as 18. She squeezes along above him in a spiral without much noise. His footsteps echo louder than he wants. At the doorway the tapping stops, and the humming stops a couple of seconds later. The room goes silent. Walker holds at the doorway, because crossing would make him visible in the small one-room cavern.

plotSections.title: Vecna in the vision room
bullets: Peeking in, Walker recognizes the room from the vision with Emhet: a smaller area and a larger roost. The smaller side has changed slightly. A square stone slab table holds crumbling maps that are nearly dust, and small figurines used as markers for military planning. One figurine hovers above the table in a hand.

The hand is an alchemical or mechanical replacement, like Walker’s own, for an arm and hand lost in a battle over an item the party reached first. Seated there, sullen and white, with a vague amused smile, is Vecna. He dragged one of three stone chairs over through the dust; one chair is overturned and another is against the back wall.

Vecna says it took Walker much longer than he expected, and asks if Walker has come to help retrieve his book. Walker says no, thanks him for asking, and steps fully into the room. The scene cuts there.

plotSections.title: The door into the abyss
bullets: Gerk pulls the latch. A thunderous sucking noise erupts, and an inky black tentacle takes him at full force, wrapping his leg, while two more slide out the sides. There is a deathly scream. Carlkin looks once and dives into the nearest pile of books, later hiding behind a box.

Gerk tries to slam the door. The spectral, oily black tentacles block it. The door hits them with a wet-meat sound, and the grip on his leg tightens. The other two tentacles search the room. Each is about a foot across at the octopus-like tips, thicker toward the door, semi-translucent, like Cthulhu-horror flesh mixed with black oil or liquefied shadow. The DM frames the opening as a dark hole of the abyss.
Ord casts Hold Monster (DC 18). The creature shrugs it off, immune to paralysis. The loose tentacles flail, and combat starts.

Ord’s proficiency bonus of +6 applies to initiative for living allies he can see, including Carlkin, and not to the creature. Rough order: Sylan 26, Gerk 25, Carlkin 25 acting after Gerk because his Dexterity is lower, Dana 22, Ord 21, creature 19. Sylan asks whether the person sleeping in the corner gets the same bonus; that is not answered.

plotSections.title: Cutting the tentacles
bullets: Gerk is grappled about the waist, not restrained: movement 0, weapon undrawn. Breaking free would take his action, though the DM provisionally allows replacing one attack if he takes the Attack action.

Sylan draws his cutting magic greatsword instead of his psychic sword, which does not cut, and uses a maneuvering strike so Dana can back up half her movement. He deals 26 slashing plus 3 radiant (29 total) to the tentacle grappling Gerk. Ichor sprays and the tentacle flexes, but only his last attack seems to actually damage it. Dana retreats.

Gerk, still weaponless and grappled, peeks past the tentacle with only his eyes. Beyond it are thousands of eyeballs staring back. He pulls back and warns the others not to look. Dana notes the warning, and it is called the void. Gerk makes a Wisdom save of 24 (a 19 plus his bonus, described as +5 Charisma to saves) and succeeds. For a moment his vision hard-zooms into one eye among the thousands, as if his mind were about to breach that reality. The pupil is shaped like a small, light-complexioned figure. He catches nothing more, but the gaze was unfavorable and he nearly lost himself.

Carlkin demands to know why Gerk opened a door straight to the abyss in his shop. Gerk says he can open doors anywhere but does not know how the power works, and that he has tested it before. Carlkin protests that this test hit his shop and his books.

A tentacle rakes the room on a legendary action, scattering books, and lashes Sylan and Gerk. A 29 hits Sylan; his Strength save of 22 succeeds, and he takes 14 bludgeoning. A separate hit, reported as 24, strikes Gerk. Gerk rages as a bonus action before the damage and takes 9 bludgeoning. The two hits were rolled differently, so his damage is not simply half of Sylan’s. From behind the books, Carlkin throws a book at the slumbering pile and shouts for the “tin can” to wake up, saying hooligans summoned the beast and they need its help. The book clangs off something metal in the corner.

plotSections.title: Ord against the extraplanar tentacles
bullets: The party is in melee with a god-tier extraplanar creature whose tentacles are coming through the hole. Dana is about fifteen feet back. Ord is beside Sylan and has already been hit; one tentacle is grasping Gerk and another has lashed Sylan. Sylan suggests Fireball. Dana refuses because it would burn Carlkin’s books, and she confirms they are fighting a god-tier monster.
Dana casts Sacred Flame. The creature’s Dexterity save of 23 succeeds and the spell does nothing. She sidesteps out of range and gives Ord inspiration.

Ord spends his last 5th-level slot to cast Holy Weapon (concentration) on Watcher’s Mantle. The DM confirms the beast is not from this plane, and the sword is buzzing hard. He hits with a 24. Mantle damage is 16, plus 15 because the target is extraplanar, and he smites with a 4th-level slot (5d8, another 21). The blow is a mostly radiant, lightsaber-like arc that severs the tentacle holding Gerk. The cut end flails; the rest collapses like stagnant water into a puddle of semi-tacky black goo, thicker than water and closer to frog spawn than tar, severed from the hole.

The DM first says seven more tentacles, then confirms two are still coming through the opening. Ord swings the mantle at the one on Sylan, spends the inspiration to land the hit, and smites again with another 4th-level slot. The blow cuts away most of that tentacle, but it stays intact and the strike is less bright than the first. Across the turn he deals over a hundred damage, with his bonus action already used.

A tentacle tries to grapple Ord. His Athletics ties the contest and the tie goes to him, so it wraps him and then falls away without holding. A second tentacle still hits him twice, for 19 and 12 bludgeoning.
Sylan uses Sentinel when Ord is hit and crits the wounded tentacle with his +1 greatsword for 29 damage including radiant. The blade cleaves it further, but tendrils still hold it together.

plotSections.title: The last tendrils and the gale
bullets: On his turn the tentacles are only flailing, and none are currently grappling. Sylan stays on the wounded one. Flanking is impossible because it is a tentacle coming out of a door. A hit for 21 damage shears one set of dark tendrils off the connecting point and splatters the room with black ichor, leaving one tentacle and an ominously cracked door.

He spends a Distracting Strike so the next ally to hit the remaining tentacle has advantage, a Trip Attack he expects will not matter because the thing is very large, and a class resource he calls a warp priest point for a final slash. Across three hits he deals 75 damage. The last tendrils break. A stump wriggles in the doorway and the rest falls and splatters. He had been weighing Action Surge and does not need it. He warns Carlkin he is in the splash zone. Carlkin beelines for the stairs and may move up to half his movement.

Gerk is next and floats opening another door so the doors could fight, or going three doors down. That does not happen. The door slams shut. At the end of Sylan’s turn it uses a legendary action, flies open, and a gale-force wind blows out. Behind it is nothing but a wall of eyes.

plotSections.title: Wall of eyes
bullets: Dana, who had moved as far away as she could, and Carlkin, already running, are not fully exposed. Sylan, Gerk, and Ord, standing adjacent, must make Wisdom saves. The effect is a magical mental ability, not sleep and not charm or fear.

Sylan uses Indomitable and saves with a 25. Gerk saves with a 23. Ord rolls a 17, fails, and is overcome. Sylan hopes a holy sword, disease immunity, or Cleansing Touch would have protected him. They do not stop this effect.

Ord is an Oath of the Watchers paladin, previously Oath of Vengeance. He uses Vigilant Rebuke: when a creature he can see succeeds on the mental save, he can strike the source, and the source does not need to be within a set distance. He asks to apply it to both allies who saved. The DM agrees the feature works, but it is a reaction, so it triggers only once. It deals 14 damage, and several eyes on the very edge of the door pop.

plotSections.title: Ord drawn into the door
bullets: Sylan and Gerk watch Ord step forward, find a gap between the eyes with his hand, and begin to pass into the wall. His mind is elsewhere. The scene with him is taken off the recorded channel, so what he experiences is not captured here.

On Gerk’s turn, Ord is being sucked bodily into the door, into a wall of eyes just inside it. The eyes focus on him and their pupils track him as he enters. He babbles incoherently about sea breezes and “my strength.” Sylan reads the babble as Ord voicing what he has lost. The tentacle that had grappled Gerk is already cut away. What remains is the door, Ord being pulled into it, and the wall of eyes.

Gerk tries to stop him by breaking the floor under him and pulling him down so he cannot walk into the mass. The floor is a cobble layer over a granular base, not solid stone all the way down. Raging, Gerk hits it with his hammer (attack 15 against an inanimate object, 16 damage, plus extra from rage) and breaks up the cobbles. Ord begins to stumble. The hand and arm already sucked into the mass hold him up somewhat. Gerk’s Strength (Athletics) is 27. An oddly hollow sucking pop accompanies the pull. Gerk goes about five feet under the floor and throws Ord into the earth so nothing can pass farther. Ord is left standing in a roughly four-to-five-foot hole with his head and shoulders above ground, and Gerk holds him so he cannot walk farther into the door. Sylan asks that the door be closed. Gerk does not close it.

plotSections.title: The doorway resists Dispel Magic
bullets: Carlkin’s footsteps fade as he runs upstairs.

Dana is left with a square-outline doorway that does not clearly reflect what is behind it, full of eyes, with Gerk in the hole and Sylan adjacent. She casts Dispel Magic at 5th level to force the door closed. It has no effect.
She considers Grasping Vine and rejects it, unwilling to pull Ord, or whatever is in the door, out of the doorway. She gives Sylan Bardic Inspiration.

plotSections.title: The eyes offer Ord his past
bullets: Ord succeeds on a Wisdom save (23). Each blink shows him the edge of a dock with a younger dragonborn standing before him. A repeating, melancholy, reverberating voice says they will show him his past if he gives them his future.
At the end of his turn several eyes swivel 180 degrees into white orbs. A red glow rises from the dark gaps, and some eyes pop or blink out of existence.

Sylan holds that Gerk has to be the one to end this, recalling that he could not interact with Gerk’s door on the boat. He does not try to close or stab the door. The eyes sit as a wall just inside the far side of the doorway, so the door still seems able to close. A reddish glow is coming from the depths.

Sylan casts Beacon of Hope on friendly creatures in range, granting advantage on Wisdom saves and death saving throws, and steps to the side of the door rather than standing in front of it. More eyes blink out, the light intensifies, and a deep cosmic voice speaks from the depths of the abyss.

chronologicalEvents: Sylan recaps the earlier boat incident: the crew shouted and rocked the boat, Ord’s dispel magic ended the party’s invisibility and silence, and the party used their communication items.
The DM confirms the spectral door is still following them and that they are still searching for a phylactery while flying home to meet Walker.
Sylan names Carlkin and Benji as possible leads, and Nyx as the fallback he wants to avoid.

The DM notes the olive oil effect and the giant constrictor snake, then places Walker at Haven Hold, leaving Hanzuni’s hoard room exhausted from training, with no set meeting with Elrus or Araden, while the others sail with the door behind them toward the stronghold. Regrouping is about a week for the party and roughly a month for Walker.

On the ship, Gerk confirms Dana can see the glowing door. She calls him the Doorman and suggests closing it; he refuses to use it on the boat. The door is a shut, corporeal, frameless, translucent spectral door with no writing. The party agrees not to use it aboard, to give it about four hours, and to keep sailing toward the stronghold.

Sylan tells Dana the earlier dispel may have been on the door or only on the party. Dana reasons that a dispel on the door itself should have stopped it leading anywhere, and that further Dispel Magic may not dismiss a door created when Ord tried to open one, or only thought of one, because the effect is keystone-level Doorman magic rather than an ordinary spell. They postpone any test or dispel until they are on solid ground. Sylan keeps the boat flying.

The DM jumps the journey ahead. About a day after the door appeared, near the same time of day, it vanishes. Gerk feels briefly more vulnerable, then that passes, and the space-warping effect is gone. The party treats its duration as about a day. Gerk checks his watch, struggles to read it, and concludes it is moving.

The rest of the five-day autumn crossing of the Twin Peaks is quiet. They reach harvest-time Langdale: harvest-ready crops, tomato fields around a familiar hut, caravans from New Navel at their tavern and traffic toward the Rita area, and new fishing boats on the glassy lake. They circle and land at the stronghold.

With about two days before Walker returns, Sylan recruits Gerk, Dana, and Ord to visit Carlkin in the tower. He may also look for Benji about the hunt, practice doors in private, and study his relic. Walker does not go; after Plymouth Gawater finishes his errand, Walker will join Elrus and Araden and continue to the training grounds.

The training grounds are young Grixto’s secret hideaway, where he lured and killed guild companions, including Tunimus, and harvested their Al Kurin to amplify his power, before Elrus and Araden ended that group. Emhet’s vision, through a legend-lore-like effect associated with Dana, showed him there with Al Kurin. Sylan tells Walker to retreat if Grixto is present.

Walker meets Araden and Plymouth Gawater and they leave Sunder for a mundane floating training island between the Lost Isles, Camp Two, and the Howling Tunnels. Seven of their days equal one day for the others. The island has a grassy training field, a ruined foundation, a western cliff plateau, roost-caves of many sizes that do not connect through the mountain, and a crumbled stronghold.

Elrus mind-whispers that the ruin was the guild hall and that Grixto’s cavern is likely entered from behind or underneath. Walker rolls a 21 Perception, sets the roost-caves off the training field, recalls the Emhet vision of people leaving a humble dwelling rather than a cave to seek guests, and finds a hidden footpath into a narrow crevice between the field and the rocky underside, large enough for a medium or possibly large dragon.

Walker enters the crack. Araden waits outside. Glimmen may not fit. Plymouth, outside the mental conversation and warned not to go far, goes to search the rune-marked stronghold for leftover artifacts and will regroup at the crack. Elrus stays outside as a mental relay: Walker taps his head and is told to call mentally instead of using flags, because there is no line of sight, and Araden would be slow to dig the crevice open. The scene pauses on Walker.

Ord, Sylan, Gerk, and Dana reach Carlkin’s lighthouse in New Navel. Signs in several languages, which Carlkin says he wrote in sixteen, forbid loitering and require appointments. Gerk reads one as "Knock loud. Be let in." and hammers the door until the boards crack. Carlkin yells from inside, denies knowing them, and says they have no appointment.

Another blow throws the door open onto crates and books, knocking Carlkin back as he holds it. He says the signs do not say what Gerk read. Gerk says Sylan wanted to talk and jokes about Sylan’s small arms. Sylan calls Gerk their ambassador and asks to discuss matters of great importance. Carlkin still refuses without an appointment and cannot hold Gerk back, so Gerk walks into the ground floor.
The ground floor is a clutter of books, maps, barrels, porridge bowls, a spiral stair, Sea of Nyx papers including a first edition the party was part of and later papers, and a snoring pile of books.

Sylan checks with Ord and Dana. They agree not to hide their relics: Carlkin has been useful and trustworthy, and Dana and Ord say he was one of the original holders. The door shuts behind them almost by itself, and Carlkin demands the useful knowledge immediately.
Gerk opens an undirected Door in Carlkin’s living room and rolls 68 on a d100 table described as all ocean. Where it leads is not shown yet.

The scene returns to Walker in the cliffside crevice. Glimmen squeezes in after him. The tunnel smells of fresh death. Glimmen says she thought the roost was unused. Elrus tells Walker there has been no trainee for centuries, that only one person used the crevice, that he learned of it from a friend’s vision, and that nothing there should be dead. Elrus agrees to bring Plymouth.
Walker draws his bow and advances. Glimmen prepares her fiery breath. He hears two-toned stone tapping and a faint hum from the cavern.

Walker sneaks toward the entrance at disadvantage and rolls a 10. Glimmen, crawling at disadvantage through the spiral cave, rolls a 19 while Walker’s footsteps echo. The tapping and then the humming stop as he reaches the doorway, leaving the room silent.

Walker peeks into the cavern from Emhet’s vision: a dragon roost, a slab map table, crumbling maps, military planning figurines, and Vecna seated in a dragged stone chair among three, holding a hovering figurine in a prosthetic hand. Vecna says Walker took longer than expected and asks if he came to help retrieve Vecna’s book. Walker refuses and enters the room.

The scene cuts back to Carlkin’s lighthouse. Gerk pulls the unseen door open. A huge sucking noise brings foot-thick, oily, semi-translucent ink-or-shadow tentacles with octopi-like ends, thickening toward a dark hole of the abyss. One wraps Gerk’s leg, two more enter, something screams, and the free tentacles search the room. Carlkin screams and dives behind a pile of books. Gerk slams the door into the tentacles, but it does not shut.

Ord’s Hold Monster at DC 18 fails because the creature is immune to paralysis. Initiative: Sylan 26, Gerk 25, Carlkin 25, Dana 22, Ord 21, creature 19. Ord’s +6 proficiency bonus applies to allies he chooses, including Carlkin, who hides behind a box and is placed after Gerk.

Sylan attacks the tentacle grappling Gerk with his magic +1 greatsword, uses Maneuvering Strike so Dana can retreat half her movement, and deals 29 damage (26 slashing, 3 radiant). Only the last attack seems to hurt it, and ichor flies. Gerk is grappled but not restrained, with movement 0, and must use his action to break free unless he can otherwise end the grapple. He is weaponless.

Gerk peeks through the door and sees thousands of eyes. He succeeds on a Wisdom save taken as 24, resists being pulled into one eye whose pupil is a small light-complexioned figure, and nearly loses himself. He warns the party not to look through the door, and Dana acknowledges it.

Carlkin protests that Gerk opened the door to the abyss in his shop. A legendary tentacle scatters his books and lashes Sylan and Gerk. Sylan is hit by a 29, succeeds on a Strength save of 22, and takes 14 bludgeoning. Gerk rages, is hit by a 24, and takes 9 bludgeoning. Carlkin throws a book to wake a metal sleeper in the corner, calling the party hooligans who summoned the beast.

Dana, about fifteen feet away, refuses to Fireball the tentacles so Carlkin’s books are not burned. Her Sacred Flame fails when the creature passes a Dexterity save on a 23. She steps out of range, grants Bardic Inspiration, and turns the turn over to Ord.

Ord casts Holy Weapon on the Watcher’s Mantle with his last 5th-level slot; the weapon reacts because the creature is extraplanar. He hits for 16 plus 15, adds 21 from a 4th-level smite, and severs the tentacle grasping Gerk. The stump flails and the rest splashes down as black, frog-spawn-like goo. Two tentacles are still coming through the opening after one each had struck Sylan and Gerk.

Ord attacks the tentacle on Sylan with inspiration and a 4th-level smite, dealing about 45 damage and over a hundred for the turn. Most of that tentacle is severed, but it remains intact. He cannot spend leftover movement to stomp it; his bonus action and reaction are already used. A gooey tentacle then tries to grapple him. He contests with Athletics 25, the tie goes to him, and the tentacle wraps him and falls away without holding. A second tentacle hits him twice for 19 bludgeoning and then 12 bludgeoning.

Sylan uses Sentinel when Ord is hit, crits the wounded tentacle with his +1 greatsword for 29 damage, and tendrils still hold it. On his turn he keeps attacking the flailing tentacles. The DM rules he cannot flank a tentacle emerging from a door. A hit for 21 damage, including radiant, severs dark tendrils at the connecting point, coats the room in black ichor again, and leaves one tentacle and a cracked door.

Sylan hits the last tentacle three times for 75 damage total: Distracting Strike for 26 plus 2 radiant, so the next ally to hit it has advantage; a Trip Attack for 20 plus 3 radiant, which does not matter because the creature is too big; and another slash for 21 plus 3 radiant. The final tendrils break, a stump wriggles in the door, and the rest splatters to the floor. He tells Carlkin to take cover, and Carlkin runs for the stairs.

Gerk, next in initiative, suggests opening another door to pit the doors against each other, but he does not do it. The door slams shut, then on a legendary action flies open into a gale-force wind and a wall of eyes. The effect is a magical mental ability, not charm or sleep. Dana is far enough away not to be fully exposed, and Carlkin runs. Of the three people still adjacent, Sylan uses Indomitable and saves with a 25, Gerk saves with a 23, and Ord rolls a 17 and fails.

Ord, Oath of the Watchers, uses Vigilant Rebuke. He learns it is a reaction and can be used only once, dealing 14 radiant damage. Several eyes on the very edge of the door pop. Ord reaches into a gap between the eyes and begins to pass through while Sylan and Gerk watch. His mind is elsewhere, and that scene leaves the recorded channel.

On Gerk’s turn, Ord is being pulled into the doorway. A wall of eyes tracks him while he babbles about sea breezes and his strength. The grappling tentacle is gone. Gerk hammers the cobble floor beneath Ord, hits with a 15, and deals 16 damage, breaking up the cobbles. Ord stumbles, still held up by the arm already inside the mass. Raging, Gerk rolls a 27 Strength check, dives about five feet into the ground, pulls Ord into the hole so his head and shoulders remain above ground, and holds him there. Carlkin’s footsteps fade as he runs upstairs.

Dana faces a square outline of a doorway filled with eyes that poorly reflects what lies behind it. She casts 5th-level Dispel Magic on the door and it does nothing. She decides against Grasping Vine and gives Sylan Bardic Inspiration.

Ord makes a Wisdom save of 23. The blinking eyes show him a dock and a younger dragonborn, and a melancholy voice offers to show his past in exchange for his future. Eyes turn into white orbs, a red glow rises between them, and some eyes vanish. Sylan casts Beacon of Hope on friendlies in range and moves beside the door, leaving the front of it clear. More eyes blink out, the glow intensifies, and a deep cosmic voice rises from the abyss.

Spectral Door.existing: A frameless spectral door that followed the party, tied to Gerk's Doorman power.
notes: It followed the ship toward the stronghold as a shut, corporeal, translucent glowing door with no frame, no writing, and no other markings.
The party never opened it. Gerk refused to use it aboard after a previous use sank him and turned him invisible.
Sylan suggested leaving it alone for about four hours and, if it remained, asking the spellcasters only once they were on solid ground.
The dispel that ended the party's invisibility and silence did not remove it. Dana argued it was keystone-level Doorman magic, manifested because Ord tried to open a door or thought of one.
It lasted about a day, then vanished on its own around the same time of day it had appeared. The space-altering effect ended, and Gerk briefly felt less protected before that feeling faded.

Gerk.existing: Half-orc barbarian, Doorman, Child of the Tree, and the party's ambassador.
notes: He can see the spectral door following him, refuses to touch it on the boat, and agrees to keep sailing and report if anything changes. When it vanishes after about a day, he feels briefly more vulnerable, then the feeling fades.
He checks a watch to judge whether twelve or twenty-four hours have passed. He has trouble reading it; the watch does move.

He goes with Sylan, Dana, and Ord to Carlkin's lighthouse in New Navel. He says he can read and reads a posted notice as "Knock loud. Be let in." He knocks hard enough to crack the boards and throw the door open, rolling a 12 and treating it as a 32 Strength check. Sylan introduces him as the party's ambassador. He answers Carlkin by pointing out Sylan's arms and walks in when Carlkin tries to push him out.

In the living room he opens a door with no destination chosen, slowly in case water comes out, and rolls 68 on a d100. The opening is the abyss. He tells Carlkin he can open doors anywhere but does not know how the power works.

A tentacle grapples him about the waist. He is grappled with movement 0, and escaping costs his action. He had not drawn a weapon. He peeks through, succeeds on a Wisdom save of 24, sees thousands of eyes, nearly loses himself, and tells the others not to look. One pupil is shaped like a small light-complexioned figure.

His Charisma bonus is +5 to ability checks and saves, and Sentinel applies to his initiative. He rolls 19 and his initiative is 25 after Ord's proficiency bonus. He rages as a bonus action and takes 9 bludgeoning from a legendary tentacle attack of 24. Ord later severs the tentacle holding him.
Adjacent to the wall of eyes, he succeeds on a Wisdom save of 23 (18 plus his +5). He suggests opening a second door so the doors fight, or going three doors down. He does not close this door.

He breaks the cobbles under Ord with his hammer (attack 15, 16 damage), then on a Strength check of 27 dives about five feet under the floor and holds Ord in the hole so Ord cannot continue through the door.
personality: Uses the doorway power without yet understanding where it opens.
quotesThemes: Reads Carlkin's sign as "Knock loud. Be let in."
"I don't know where this will go. Hopefully not the ocean."
"I can open doors anywhere. I don't know how to work this power."
Warns the party not to look through the door after seeing the eyes.

Dana.existing: Half-elf cleric and Gatekeeper of the Pitel keystone.
notes: She can see the glowing door following Gerk, calls him the doorman, and tells him to close it. She argues it is keystone-level Doorman magic, possibly manifested because Ord tried to open a door or thought of one, and warns against trying to dispel it while airborne.
A legend-lore-like interaction between her and Emhet triggered the shared vision of Grixto at the training-ground hideaway with Al Kurin.
She goes with Sylan, Gerk, and Ord to Carlkin. She tells Sylan that Carlkin was one of the original holders and that they have no reason to hide their relics from him.

She stays at the back of the fight. Initiative 22 after Ord's +6. She hears the tentacles and steps back, then retreats another half of her movement when Sylan uses maneuvering strike, ending about fifteen feet from the doorway. She acknowledges Gerk's warning not to look.

She refuses to cast Fireball because it would burn Carlkin's books. Sacred Flame has no effect after the creature's Dexterity save of 23. She sidesteps out of range and uses a bonus action to give Ord inspiration, asking him to do paladin things.

She is far enough from the wall of eyes that she does not have to save. She casts 5th-level Dispel Magic on the eye-door to force it shut, and the spell has no effect. She has Grasping Vine available but will not use it, because she does not want to drag whatever is in the door out. She gives Sylan Bardic Inspiration and ends her turn.
personality: Protective of Carlkin's books even in the middle of the fight.
quotesThemes: Calls Gerk the doorman and asks why he does not just close the door.
"He was one of the original holders."
"We're not going to burn all the books."

notes: He recaps for Dana that he and Aris dispelled the party's invisibility and silence. He keeps the ship flying toward the stronghold and suggests Gerk leave the spectral door alone for about four hours, then consult the spellcasters on solid ground. He later infers that door lasted about a day.

He expects to check Carlkin and Benji for leads and otherwise return to Nyx, which he does not want to do. Once home, with about two days before Walker is expected back, he plans to visit Carlkin, possibly Benji, practice doors privately away from untrusted onlookers, and study his relic. He looks toward someone or something called Caracas while saying he does not want untrusted people watching.
He reminds Walker that the training grounds are where dragon things were stored and dragons were lured to be killed, and orders Walker and his companion to retreat if Grixto is there.

At Carlkin's lighthouse he jokes that the sign means they need an appointment, asks whether Gerk can read, and tells him to knock. He had forgotten Carlkin's voice and is not sure they have spoken before. He introduces Gerk as the party's ambassador, asks to discuss matters of great importance, and checks with Dana and Ord before sharing the relics. He then agrees to hide nothing and offers Carlkin an exchange of knowledge.
He declares that his own door opens into the room where Walker is facing Vecna, and the DM confirms that destination.

He is next closest to the tentacles after Gerk because he followed Gerk in. Initiative 26, including Ord's bonus. He sets aside his psychic sword, which does not cut, and draws his +1 magic greatsword. He deals 26 magical slashing plus 3 radiant; only the last attack damages the tentacle holding Gerk. Maneuvering strike lets Dana move half her speed away.
A legendary tentacle attack of 29 hits him. His Strength save of 22 succeeds, and he takes 14 bludgeoning. He asks whether they are fighting a god-tier monster, and Dana says yes.

With Sentinel he reacts when Ord is hit and crits that tentacle for 29 total damage, part of it radiant from a d8, leaving tendrils still holding it. He cannot flank a tentacle coming out of a door. He then deals 75 damage across three attacks: Distracting Strike so the next ally has advantage, a Trip Attack that fails because the creature is too large, and a further slash funded by a resource heard as warp priest points. That finishes the visible tendrils and leaves a wriggling stump. He warns Carlkin out of the splash zone, considers Action Surge, and does not need it.

Adjacent to the wall of eyes, he uses Indomitable and succeeds on a Wisdom save of 25. He reads Ord's babble about sea breezes and "my strength" as Ord voicing what he has lost. He asks Gerk to close the door and says Gerk has to be the one to end it, remembering he could not work Gerk's door on the boat.
He casts Beacon of Hope on friendly creatures in range, giving advantage on Wisdom saves and death saving throws, and moves to the side of the door in case something tries to come through.

Ord.existing: Dragonborn Oath of the Watchers paladin and Gatekeeper of Feldspar.
notes: He cast the dispel magic that removed the party's invisibility and silence. Dana says the spectral door appeared because he tried to open a door or thought about one.
He goes with Sylan, Gerk, and Dana to Carlkin. He says Carlkin has been a useful resource and that the party has no reason to distrust him.

Allies he can see, including Carlkin, add his proficiency bonus to initiative. The bonus is stated as +6, and one report also treats it as +7. It covers other living creatures he can see, which he describes as even a mouse that would have to survive, and it does not apply to the enemy. His own initiative is 21, bonus already included. Sylan's 26 and Dana's 22 include this bonus.
Hold Monster against the tentacles fails. His spell save DC is 18, the creature saves, and it is immune to the paralyzed condition.

He spends his last 5th-level spell slot to cast Holy Weapon, concentrating, on the Watcher's Mantle, expecting no further fights that day. The mantle buzzes because the foe is extraplanar. An attack of 24 deals 16, plus 15 because the target is not from this plane, plus 21 from a 4th-level smite (5d8), severing the tentacle grasping Gerk in a mostly radiant arc. He then spends Dana's inspiration and another 4th-level smite on the tentacle attacking Sylan. That second blow is dimmer, removes most of the tentacle, and leaves it intact. He deals over a hundred damage that turn and has already used his bonus action.

A tentacle tries to grapple him beside Sylan. His Athletics of 25 ties, and the tie goes to him, so it cannot hold him. The follow-up strikes deal 19 and then 12 bludgeoning. He has no reaction left to stomp.

He is confirmed in play as an Oath of the Watchers paladin; he previously had an Oath of Vengeance. Disease immunity, Cleansing Touch, and his holy sword do not cover this mental effect. Adjacent to the wall of eyes, he fails a Wisdom save of 17, including a +5 bonus, and expects to succumb.

Vigilant Rebuke lets him damage the source when an ally succeeds on the save, even if that source is far from him. He asks to trigger it for both successes. It costs his reaction, so he uses it once and deals 14 radiant damage, popping eyes on the edge of the door.

He steps into a gap between the eyes and is pulled bodily through. Pupils track him. He babbles incoherently about sea breezes and "my strength." After Gerk breaks the floor, the arm already inside the mass holds him up somewhat, and he is left shoulder-deep in a roughly four-to-five-foot hole, head and shoulders above ground, looking up at the doorway of eyes.
On a Wisdom save of 23, each blink shows him the edge of a dock and a younger dragonborn. A reverberating melancholy voice says they will show him his past if he gives them his future.
personality: Willing to spend his highest remaining spell slots on this fight.
quotesThemes: Incoherent babble about sea breezes and "my strength," which Sylan reads as what Ord has lost.
openQuestions: Does the metal sleeper in the corner also receive Ord's initiative bonus?

Walker.existing: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter, Gatekeeper of The Reach, bonded to Glimmen.
notes: He leaves Hanzuni's hoard room at Haven Hold on his own training schedule, with no meeting time set with Elrus or Araden. The regimen has given him one level of exhaustion and disadvantage on ability checks.

About a week of travel for the party is roughly a month for him under a sevenfold time difference. The others are flying home to meet him. From the party's side at the stronghold, he is expected back in about two days, and Sylan treats an earlier check-in as evidence he is fine.

He does not go to Carlkin. He meets Elrus and Araden and, after Plymouth finishes an errand, travels with them from Sunder to the training island. He does not remember why they are going until the DM restores the Grixto hideaway lead. Sylan has told him to retreat rather than fight if Grixto is there.

He rolls a 21 on Perception, finds the hidden ledge and crevice, and investigates. He leaves Araden outside, Elrus as a mental relay, and Plymouth searching the guild stronghold with orders not to wander too far. He signals Elrus by tapping his head.

He climbs the narrow cliff path into the crevice with his bow drawn, stalking the smell of death. His passive Perception is 18. He hears faint humming and two different stones tapping. He confirms with Elrus that the place should have been unused for centuries, then has Elrus bring Plymouth down while he continues.

He approaches the roost with Glimmen and fails a disadvantaged Stealth check with a 10; his footsteps echo. He recognizes the cavern as the room from Emhet's vision. The smaller side has changed slightly since that vision. He refuses Vecna's request to help retrieve a book and walks in.
His own arm and hand are a replacement, compared directly to Vecna's alchemical or mechanical replacement. Both losses are tied to a battle over an item the party reached first.
personality: Nervous about being alone with only Glimmen, and unwilling to stay alone with Vecna or help him.
quotesThemes: Tells Vecna he has not come to help retrieve the book.

Hanzuni.existing: Ancient copper dragon and hoard master of Haven Hold, who loans gold for quests.
notes: Walker has just spoken with him in the hoard room at Haven Hold and is leaving. The DM calls him the hoard master of Haven Hold.

Carlkin.existing: Elderly turtle-like original holder who lives in a lighthouse in New Navel.
notes: Sylan hopes he has a lead. During the two days before Walker is expected back, Sylan, Gerk, Dana, and Ord visit him. He is at his lighthouse in New Navel, which the party has entered once or twice, and is present for the fight. He is not away in Langdale.

His weathered wooden door carries mixed-script notices, including no loitering and appointments only. He says he wrote them in sixteen languages and expects visitors to read at least one. He rejects Gerk's reading of "Knock loud. Be let in." After the third blow he shouts to stop breaking the door, says he does not know any "girls," and refuses them for lack of an appointment. He is holding the door when Gerk throws it open into crates and books.

He calls himself very busy with studying and other appointments and tries and fails to shove Gerk back out. Dana says he was one of the original holders. Ord says he has been a useful resource and that the party has no reason to distrust him. Sylan is not sure they have actually talked before and had forgotten his voice. They agree not to hide their relics. He demands Sylan get to the point.

The ground floor is cluttered with crates, barrels, maps, tomes, porridge bowls, and papers, including a first edition of the Sea of Nyx that the party was part of, later additions, and very old tomes. A pile of books in the corner is snoring. The door swings shut behind the party almost by itself. A spiral staircase is on the far wall.

When the doorway opens onto the abyss he screams, dives behind the books, and is furious that Gerk tested the power in the shop. A tentacle scatters his books. He throws a book at the metal sleeper in the corner, calls it a tin can, and yells for it to wake because hooligans summoned the beast.

He is treated as an ally. He receives Ord's initiative bonus, rolls 25, and acts after Gerk because of lower Dexterity. When Sylan warns him out of the splash zone, he runs for the stairs and is allowed up to half his movement. He is already running when the wall of eyes appears, so he does not make the Wisdom save. His footsteps fade as he goes upstairs.
personality: Irritable and pedantic with unannounced visitors, and protective of his books once the doorway lets the beast in.
quotesThemes: "What are you doing? Stop trying to break down my door."
"I do not know any girls."
"No appointment."
"Can you not read? I wrote it in sixteen different languages."
"I am a very busy individual. I have much studying to do."
"Let's see it then."
"You didn't tell me you can open a door straight to the abyss."
"Wake up you tin can. These hooligans have summoned the beast and we need your help."

Benji.existing: Familiar with The Reach and may be at the party's bar.
notes: Sylan thinks Benji may have a lead once the party is home and wants to question him about what they are hunting if he is in town. The party does not confirm that he is there.

Nyx.existing: A location that may hold hobgoblins who know where the lich is hiding.
notes: Sylan does not want to go, but he believes the party has to return to Nyx if Carlkin, Benji, and the other leads produce nothing.

constrictor snake.existing: A summoned constrictor snake that follows Dana at her command.
notes: The DM confirms the giant constrictor snake is still summoned while checking the party's current state on the ship.

Langdale.existing: Forested home region identified by its flora, fauna, and landmarks.
notes: The party reaches it after five days through the Twin Peaks and finds it in harvest. Crops are ready, a familiar hut is surrounded by small tomato fields, and the glassy lake has more fishing vessels working the coves.
Trade caravans run from New Navel to the party's tavern, and some traffic still runs to and from the Rita area.

Doorman.existing: Gerk's Doorman role and doorway ability.
notes: Dana treats the lingering spectral door as a product of this role and does not expect ordinary Dispel Magic to dismiss keystone-level Doorman magic. That door lasted about a day and ended on its own.

Gerk can open a door without choosing a destination. The opening in Carlkin's lighthouse, a d100 roll of 68, led to the abyss. Fifth-level Dispel Magic did not close or dismiss it, and Sylan could not end it. Sylan treats these doorways as Gerk's to close.
openQuestions: How does Gerk's door choose its destination? A d100 of 68 was described as a table of all ocean, but the opening led to the abyss.

Grixto.existing: Mobile antagonist seeking Al Kurin, hiding a phylactery among mundane possessions.
notes: As a younger dragon he kept a secret hideaway at the dragon-rider training grounds. He lured guild companions there, killed them, and took their Al Kurin to amplify his power. He killed Tunimus and another figure whose name the DM could not recall, described as possibly Tunimus's right hand.
Elrus and Araden then brought that group down.
Emhet's vision showed him there, sitting with a couple of Al Kurin and plotting his next steps, then walking out of a humble dwelling as if looking for guests.

Elrus suspects the cavern is entered from the backside or underneath the cliff, through a narrow crevice and hidden footpath, rather than from the open roosts facing the training field. Walker's memory of the vision cuts against a simple cave exit.

Galixtar.existing: A dragon associated with Grixto and being hunted by the party.
notes: The DM says Galixtar is probably the one who used this crevice the way a younger dragon could, tucking its wings, hopping out, and flying clear. Glimmen has to squeeze.
Elrus says only one person used the place and that there has been no trainee there in centuries.

Al Kurin.existing: Vessels containing the souls of dragons.
notes: Described as a dragon's heart of hearts. Grixto took them from guild companions he killed at the training grounds and used them to amplify his power.
In Emhet's vision he sat with a couple of Al Kurin while plotting his next steps.

Dragon Rider Training Grounds.existing: Dragon Rider guild training grounds on a small floating island near the Lost Isles.
notes: A small, otherwise ordinary floating island between the Lost Isles, Camp Two, and the Howling Tunnels, in a mountainous region between three islands. Travel from Sunder takes seven days for the travelers and one day for people remaining behind.

Most of the island is a flat field of thick grass. The western side is a plateau and cliffs. A crumbling foundation, the old guild stronghold, overlooks the field. Elrus identifies the ruin as the guild hall, crumbled from time and disuse. Expansive runes mark the ruins. Plymouth wonders whether any artifacts remain.
Cliff caves are open roosts, not through-tunnels, from small-stable size up to the entrance of Araden's roost, used to shelter dragons and trainees.

A thin crevice between the rocky underside and the field, reached by a concealed footpath, can admit a medium dragon and possibly a large one, with a short bound from the crack onto the field. Elrus believes this backside or underside is the way into Grixto's cavern. It is the secret hideaway where young Grixto gathered and killed guild dragons for their Al Kurin.

Walker, Elrus, Araden, Plymouth, and Glimmen investigate it. If Grixto is present they are to retreat. The crevice leads to the roost from Emhet's vision, slightly changed into a smaller planning area plus a larger dragon roost, where Vecna is waiting.

Elrus.existing: Walker's hidden ally in the coming confrontation.
notes: With Araden, he brought about the end of Grixto's group after Grixto killed the guild dragons at the training grounds.

He travels with Walker to the training island and speaks into Walker's mind while the wind howls. He identifies the crumbled structure as the guild hall and suspects Grixto's cavern is reached from the backside or underneath.

He offers to enter the crack or act as a relay, and stays outside as the relay. Flag signals will not work without line of sight, so he tells Walker to call mentally. He says he can intervene faster than Araden, who would take a long time to dig the crevice open.

When Walker contacts him from inside, he asks if Walker is in trouble. He says there has not been a trainee in centuries, that only one person used this place, that he did not know it was there until the vision Walker's friend presented, and that nothing dead should be down there. He agrees to get Plymouth and come down shortly.
quotesThemes: "That was the guild hall. It is crumbled with time and lack of use. I suspect Grixto's cavern is accessed from the backside or underneath."
"Just holler with your mind and we will do our best to intervene."
Asks Walker if he is in trouble.

Araden.existing: A magically capable companion brought secretly to The Reach.
notes: With Elrus, she brought about Grixto's demise. She accompanies Walker to the training island.
She cannot fit into the crevice and stays outside. She can raise a giant ruckus if Walker needs help. Digging the crevice open would take her a long time, so Elrus is the faster backup.
The largest cliff roosts are about the size of the entrance to her roost.

Emhet.existing: Deity at the gods' council who knows the party safeguards the keys.
notes: A vision received by basically everyone, triggered by Dana's legend-lore-like interaction with Emhet, showed Grixto at the training-ground hideaway with Al Kurin. The figures left a humble abode looking for guests.
The roost Walker enters is that same room, slightly changed: a smaller planning area plus a larger dragon roost. Elrus says he only learned the place existed from that vision.

Plymouth Gawater.existing: Gnome artificer and party ally guiding the new keystone keepers.
notes: Walker's group waits for him to finish an errand, then he travels with Walker and Araden from Sunder to the training island. He is not part of the mental conversation with Elrus and Araden until Walker speaks to him aloud.
He studies the island, especially the expansive runes on the stronghold, and wonders whether any artifacts remain after so long.

He splits off to search the stronghold, then regroups at the crack, and agrees not to wander too far. He says to holler if he is needed. He notes the crack looks too small to assume Glimmen can enter and suggests Araden raise a ruckus from outside if needed. Elrus later goes to bring him down into the crevice.
personality: Curious about the ruins, runes, and leftover artifacts, and cautious about the crack.

Langdale Stronghold.existing: Party's central stronghold and home base.
notes: The party lands here with about two days before Walker is expected back. Sylan wants door practice kept inside, out of sight of people they do not trust.

Killed by Grixto after Grixto amplified his power with stolen Al Kurin. The DM also alluded to a second victim, possibly Tunimus's right hand, whose name he could not recall. Their group then met its end at the hands of Elrus and Araden.
She enters the crevice with Walker by crawling and squeezing. She cannot fly in or out. Backtracking means squeezing under her. A younger dragon could tuck, hop out, and fly.
Over the mind link she says she thought the place was unused and that the death smells fresh. She grumbles at the smell and readies her fiery breath as Walker advances.
While crawling she must use Stealth at disadvantage. She has no Stealth bonus; the check is Dexterity. She rolls a 19 counted as 18 and works along above Walker in a spiral without making much noise.
quotesThemes: Asks Walker if he smells it, and says she thought this place was unused and that the death smells fresh.

notes: Sylan plans to spend part of the two downtime days getting to know his relic and learning to use it better.
Ord, Sylan, Gerk, and Dana enter New Navel and go to Carlkin's lighthouse, a place they have been inside once or twice.
Trade caravans run from New Navel to the party's tavern in Langdale.

Door.existing: The doorway Gerk opened in Carlkin's lighthouse, a supernatural passage between places.
notes: Gerk opens it on the ground floor with no destination in mind, slowly in case water comes out, and rolls 68 on a d100. One description calls that table all ocean. The opening is a dark hole of the abyss.
Opening it makes a thunderous sucking noise. Oily black tentacles pour through and physically block him from slamming it shut.

Looking through it forces a Wisdom save. Past the tentacles are thousands of staring eyes. One pupil is shaped like a small light-complexioned figure. The view nearly pulls the viewer into that reality.

After the tendrils are cut, it slams shut, then flies open on a gale-force wind. It then looks like a weird square outline more than a solid door, filled with eyes, and does not clearly reflect what is behind it. A wall of eyes sits just inside.
Fifth-level Dispel Magic does not close or dismiss it. Gerk does not close it. Sylan says only Gerk can end this doorway.

Ord finds a gap between the eyes and is pulled through, which makes an oddly hollow sucking pop. The eyes blink him visions of a dock and a younger dragonborn and offer his past in exchange for his future. They then swivel into white orbs, a red glow builds in the dark between them, and eyes pop and blink out as the light intensifies. A deep cosmic voice speaks from the abyss. The doorway still appears closable.
quotesThemes: "We will show you your past if you give us your future."
openQuestions: A d100 of 68 was described as a table of all ocean, but this opening led to the abyss. How that roll maps to the destination is unresolved.

Sea of Nyx.existing: A written chronicle. One report heard the title as Sea of Nyxs.
notes: Carlkin has papers the DM calls a first edition of the Sea of Nyx, which the party was part of, mixed on his tables with newer pages of various ages and much older tomes.

Carlkin's lighthouse.existing: Carlkin's home in New Navel, also described as his bookshop.
notes: The party has been inside once or twice. The ground floor is crowded with crates, barrels, maps, books, porridge bowls, and papers, with a pile directly behind the door and a spiral staircase on the far wall.
The weathered door can swing shut almost on its own. Gerk opens his abyss door in this room, and the fight with the tentacles and the wall of eyes happens here.

Vecna.existing: Elder god of liches who watches from the periphery.
notes: He is already waiting in the dragon roost from Emhet's vision, seated at a square slab table of crumbling maps and military-planning figurines. One figurine hovers in his hand. The tapping stops as Walker reaches the door, and a faint humming stops seconds later.
His face is sullen and white, with amusement under a vague smile. He sits in a stone chair he dragged through the dust. Of the three chairs, one is overturned and one is against the back wall.
His hand and arm are an alchemical or mechanical replacement for a limb lost in a battle over an item the party reached first. The DM compares that replacement to Walker's own.
He expected Walker sooner and asks Walker to help retrieve his book. Walker refuses. The book is not identified.
personality: Sullen, vaguely smiling, and mocking while he waits.
quotesThemes: "Took you much longer than I thought it would."
"Have you come to help me retrieve my book?"
openQuestions: Which book is Vecna asking Walker to help retrieve?

Abyssal eye-beast.existing: The extraplanar creature beyond Gerk's door, seen as oily tentacles and then a wall of eyes.
notes: It is a god-tier monster and explicitly not from this plane. The party likens it to a kraken and excludes it from Ord's ally bonus. Carlkin calls it the beast the doorway summoned into his shop. Dana agrees with Sylan that it is god-tier. Watcher's Mantle buzzes and deals extra damage because the target is extraplanar.

Its initiative is 19. Three oily, semi-translucent black tentacles pour from the opening. One grapples Gerk about the waist. The others search the room and flail. The tips are about a foot across, octopus-like, and grow thicker toward the door. They read as liquefied shadow or ink. They are corporeal: the door strikes them with a wet-meat sound. They cannot be flanked, because they are appendages coming out of a door.
It is immune to the paralyzed condition, so Hold Monster does not stick. Sacred Flame does nothing after its Dexterity save of 23.

A legendary action lashes two creatures. An attack of 29 hits Sylan for 14 bludgeoning after his Strength save of 22. An attack of 24 hits raging Gerk for 9 bludgeoning. A grapple against Ord fails when Ord's Athletics of 25 ties and wins the tie. Follow-up hits deal 19 and 12 bludgeoning.

The tendril mass is bigger than Large. Damaged tendrils can look like they reform, and the mass is too big for Sylan's trip to treat it as a normal foe. When severed, the cut end flails and the rest falls like stagnant water, splashing into semi-tacky black goo with the consistency of frog spawn. Ichor coats the room. Ord fully severs the tentacle holding Gerk. The tentacle on Sylan is mostly severed and stays intact on remaining tendrils until Sylan's later round finishes the visible tendrils, leaving a stump wriggling in the door.

Behind the tentacles are thousands of staring eyes. One pupil is shaped like a small, light-complexioned figure. After the tendrils are destroyed, the opening shows nothing but that wall of eyes. Creatures adjacent to it must make a Wisdom save. The effect is a magical mental ability. It is not sleep, and it is not charm or fear. Gerk saves with a 24 on the first look and a 23 against the wall. Sylan saves with a 25 using Indomitable. Ord fails with a 17 and is drawn in through a gap while the pupils track him. Edge eyes pop when Ord's Vigilant Rebuke deals 14 radiant damage.

The eyes blink Ord a dock and a younger dragonborn, then offer his past in exchange for his future. They swivel 180 degrees into white orbs, a red glow builds between them, and eyes pop and blink out as the light intensifies. A deep cosmic voice speaks from the abyss.
